newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler plays down prosecutor's probe.
newsitem.headline: Daimler plays down prosecutor's probe.

text.p: German prosecutors said on Thursday they were investigating a senior executive of Daimler-Benz AG for allegedly infringing rules on the disclosure of earnings.

The probe refers to remarks made at the Geneva auto show by management board member Eckard Cordes who told reporters Daimler's group 1996 net profit would be more than 2 billion marks and sales would total around 107 billion marks.
The profit figure he cited was well above analysts' expectations and Daimler's share price rose by more than 3.5 percent the next day.

"The investigation refers to the alleged passing on of insider knowledge," a spokesman for the prosecutors' office told Reuters. "A figure was cited in Geneva which had potential impact on the share price."
A Daimler spokesman played down the investigation.
"This is a routine matter for the Federal Securities Supervision Authority to consider if a punishable action (has been committed)," a company spokesman said.
The prosecutors' spokesman said the office had started the investigation in response to a legal complaint filed by the Federal Securities Supervision Authority, or BAWe.
Cordes made the remarks at a dinner in Geneva on March 3. Daimler went on to report 1996 group net income of 2.8 billion marks in April, a turnaround from a loss of 5.7 billion marks.

The BAWe announced in March it was investigating the case to establish whether the disclosure should have come via a so- called "ad-hoc" electronic transmission, which German law requires for potentially market-moving information.
Failure to report via the "ad-hoc" route sometimes consitutes a violation of Germany's insider trading rules.
